newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo stocks post healthy gains on strong 'tankan'.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo stocks post healthy gains on strong 'tankan'.

text.p: Tokyo stocks posted healthy gains by Wednesday's close as investor confidence in Japan's economic outlook was wafted higher by a surprisingly strong improvement in business sentiment shown in the key "tankan" survey by the Bank of Japan, brokers said.
But market participants are willing to wait for forthcoming economic indicators to make sure of an uptrend in the economy before testing a key 21,000 point in the Nikkei 225 stock index, they said.
The 225-share Nikkei average rose 337.34 points or 1.66 percent to close at 20,679.27. Its September futures added 390 points to finish at 20,760.

"The 'tankan' has soothed worries about Japan's feeble economy, while the yen rests at a comfortable level (for exporters), further supporting stocks," said Hiroyuki Nakai, chief investment strategist at Nikko Securities Co Ltd.
The quarterly tankan report's diffusion index for big manufacturers rose to plus seven in June from plus two in March, when the previous survey was conducted.
The figure was stronger than expected and caused a frenzy on financial markets, battering the dollar and bond prices but igniting a rally in Tokyo stocks.
The tankan fuelled speculation that the central bank may move sooner rather than later to tighten credit.
The index represents the percentage of companies which see business conditions as favourable minus the percentage of those viewing conditions as unfavourable.
